notes: No changes to the step 1 parts list.
The Nano RP2040 Connect was not found by lookup_part, so a new part type is drafted.

The breadboard coordinates are read from the image. The image's upper half (rows f-j) is bank 'b' in the catalogue naming, and the lower half (rows a-e) is bank 't'. The upper rail row next to the black line is treated as 'tn' (ground).
The pushbutton straddles the centre gap, with its legs in columns 8 and 10. The two top legs (side 1) are in 8b.f and 10b.f, and the two bottom legs (side 2) are in 8t.e and 10t.e.
The dark gray wire from GND goes to the upper rail at tn.1. A short dark gray wire runs from the rail at tn.7 to 10b.g, which puts the button's top side at GND.
The teal wire runs from D2 to 8t.d. That is in the same column strip as the button's bottom legs, so D2 is on side 2.
Rail hole numbers tn.1 and tn.7 are approximate positions read from the image.
There is no external resistor, because the sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP, so D2 is pulled high and pressing the button pulls it to GND.
The central board has no extra circuit. It is powered over USB and uses its onboard RGB LED.
The USB cable ports are unspecified, so those edges name only the board's USB port.
